subject: gnomeTinkerer
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: gnome tinkerer with a backpack of gadgets.
Style: whimsical low-poly mix.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the gnome identity reads well overall, but I'm spotting issues: the eyebrows cross oddly over the eyes in three-quarter view, the nose looks like a pinkish blob, and the cheek spheres seem too large, clumping awkwardly beside the nose.

For soundness, the backpack is a bigger problem — it towers above the head and the bedroll sits at head height, covering the neck/head in back view. I need to lower the pack position relative to the head and shoulders so it doesn't visually overlap the skull, adjusting the frustum box and bedroll height downward while checking it still clears the body geometry.

I'll move the bedroll to the bottom of the pack instead, swapping positions with the scroll, and recalculate so the bedroll sits near the hips rather than the neck — checking the z-depth offsets so it doesn't collide with the scroll or legs. After adjusting, the bedroll and scroll end up at distinct heights with enough clearance between them.

Trying bedroll lower at the pack bottom instead avoids the clutter, but then the scroll placement conflicts again. I think the simplest fix is dropping the scroll down to rest right at the pack's top edge, smaller and thinner so it doesn't overlap anything else.

Steam puffs are just gray disco-ball orbs floating overhead—fine. Checking the rest: arms T-pose, hands, hat tip glow disc, boot cuffs, tubular legs, hammer and wrench hanging off the belt all read fine. Eyebrows at z 0.131 sweep visibly over the eyes in close-up—also fine.

Cheeks look too lumpy, so I'm shrinking them down and softening the color, and bumping up the nose size slightly with an adjusted position so the tip pokes past the head surface, updating the nose highlight to match. Moustache still covers the mouth, the gnome sits properly on the sinking floor base, and the overall composition with props looks good—though the side view shows the backpack is sized a bit large.

I'm reworking the bedroll placement, moving it lower on the pack so it sits above the hip area without overlapping the bottom trim box, but need to watch that the scroll doesn't visually collide with the bedroll from the back view since both sit toward the rear of the pack.

So instead I'm relocating the scroll up to the pack top, resting it on the top trim near the straps, with caps and red bands positioned symmetrically. This shifts the pipe and lantern bar positions too, so I'm adjusting the pipe's base height upward since the scroll now occupies the space it used to rest on.

I'm repositioning the scroll's end caps to the new top location, moving them to y G+0.80 and z PZ-0.02 with a slightly larger radius, since this scroll piece was originally designed for the lower back but is now placed higher up.

The gear train and bedroll positions still check out fine, so I'm ready to finalize the answer.
